2609.15855.title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
2609.15855.paper_summary: People increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for mental health support, yet their safety in evolving, high-risk conversations remains poorly characterised. We developed K-Bench, a clinician-calibrated, protected benchmark evaluating 125 model configurations representing 33 base models from 14 providers across a fixed cohort of 200 multi-turn vignettes involving suicide, self-harm, domestic violence, substance misuse, and no-risk presentations. Synthetic patient conversations showed substantial distributional overlap with real human-AI conversations. A frozen GPT-4o judge achieved 94.2% exact agreement with clinician consensus across 6,751 eligible item comparisons from 151 clinician-rated transcripts. Leading models combined strong supportive conversation with combined-risk scores above 95, whereas risk exploration exposed substantial variation among lower-performing configurations. Therapeutic prompting produced configuration-specific gains concentrated among weaker models, while elevated reasoning produced no average improvement. K-Bench combines broader clinical coverage and configuration-scale comparison with a continuously updated public leaderboard whose operational test materials are protected from direct optimisation. The leaderboard is available at www.k-bench.ai.
2609.15855.paper_summary_zh: 人們越來越多地使用大型語言模型（LLMs）來支持心理健康，但它們在不斷發展的高風險對話中的安全性仍然缺乏明確的特徵。我們開發了 K-Bench，一個經過臨床醫生校準的受保護基準，評估 125 種模型配置，代表來自 14 家提供者的 33 種基礎模型，涵蓋 200 個多輪小品，涉及自殺、自我傷害、家庭暴力、物質濫用和無風險情況。合成的病人對話顯示出與真實的人類-AI 對話之間有顯著的分佈重疊。一個凍結的 GPT-4o 評審在 6,751 次合格項目比較中，與臨床醫生共識達成了 94.2% 的精確一致性，這些比較來自 151 份臨床醫生評分的轉錄本。領先的模型將強有力的支持性對話與超過 95 的綜合風險分數結合起來，而風險探索則揭示了表現較差的配置之間的顯著變異。治療性提示在較弱的模型中產生了特定配置的增益，而提高推理能力則未帶來平均改善。K-Bench 結合了更廣泛的臨床覆蓋和配置規模比較，並擁有一個不斷更新的公共排行榜，其操作測試材料受到直接優化的保護。排行榜可在 www.k-bench.ai 獲得。
